title: Define access control policy for Unit Economics dashboard (restricted pricing/discount slices)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
The internal Unit Economics dashboard is becoming the source of truth for blended cost ($/1M output tokens) and driver drilldowns. Some dashboard slices and exports expose price/discount/credits information (or allow back-solving it), which must be restricted to Finance leadership + a small set of Product owners.

Goal
Define a clear, implementable access control policy for Unit Economics dashboard views and exports, aligned with Finance leadership. Policy must be specific enough for Console + backend to enforce consistently and auditable for compliance.

Definitions (working)
- "General Unit Econ views": cost efficiency and operational drivers that do NOT expose pricing/discount/credits at account-level. Examples: blended compute+overhead per output token excluding discount/credits impact; cache hit rate; region mix; model mix.
- "Pricing-sensitive views": any view that directly shows or allows inference of discounts/credits/price overrides, including account-level slices, tier-level net revenue adjustments, or gross margin views that incorporate deal terms.
- "Export": CSV download, copy/paste table export, or API endpoint that returns row-level data beyond what’s displayed in the UI.

Proposed access control policy (to confirm)
1) Default access (Engineering + Product + SRE)
- Can view: blended $/1M output tokens at aggregated grain (daily) with drilldowns by model family/variant, region, customer tier (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise), and runtime_config/quantization_profile.
- Cannot view: any metrics including discounts/credits, net revenue, gross margin, or account-level identifiers.
- Can export: aggregated tables at supported grain with k-anonymity-like guardrails (see below).

2) Finance access (FP&A + CFO org)
- Can view: everything in default access + pricing-sensitive metrics (discount/credit impacts, net blended cost including credits policy, gross margin deltas).
- Can view: account-level slices for reconciliation workflows (requires explicit role + audit log).
- Can export: account-level reconciliation extracts (with retention + auditing).

3) Product leadership (limited)
- Can view: pricing-sensitive metrics at aggregated tier level only (no account-level). Intended for pricing/packaging decisions and routing defaults.
- Can export: aggregated tier-level views only.

4) Support/CS
- No access by default. Use Finance-exported summaries or a separate customer-facing cost reporting workflow (out of scope).

Enforcement requirements
A) RBAC model
- Use existing Console roles/groups (e.g., okta groups) as the source of truth.
- Introduce at least two new permissions:
  - unit_econ:view_pricing_sensitive (Finance + specific Product leadership)
  - unit_econ:view_account_level (Finance reconciliation only; smallest possible membership)
- Backend must enforce permissions (not just UI). Console should hide UI controls as a convenience.

B) Guardrails to prevent inference via small slices
- Minimum aggregation threshold for any slice shown/exported: if a filter results in < N distinct customers OR < M total requests, return "insufficient aggregation".
- Threshold values to be proposed by Eng + Finance (initial proposal: N=5 customers, M=500 requests) and documented.
- Enforce the same rule for exports.

C) Audit logging + retention
- Required for any access to pricing-sensitive or account-level views.
- Log: user identity, timestamp, permission used, query parameters (redacted for PII), and row counts.
- Retention: align with existing Console audit log retention for security-sensitive views.

D) Restricted fields list (must never be available without pricing-sensitive permission)
- discounts_applied_usd
- credits_applied_usd
- net_revenue_usd (or any net revenue proxy)
- gross_margin_percent / gross_margin_usd
- effective_rate_usd_per_1m_tokens (if defined as post-discount)
- customer_id, account_id, org_slug, or any account-level identifier (unless unit_econ:view_account_level)

Non-goals (for PM-484)
- Defining the canonical blended metric formula (PM-483 / ADR-0142).
- Designing the full dashboard UX (DES-211/DES-212).
- Implementing the RBAC system itself (ENG tickets + security review), though this ticket must define requirements clearly enough for implementation.

Artifacts / references
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/internal-unit-economics-dashboard-prd.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0142-blended-cost-per-1m-output-tokens-definition.json
- Security review ticket: ENG-2921

Open questions
1) Do we treat "customer tier" as pricing-sensitive? Finance requested tier-level net revenue adjustments; Product wants tier-level unit cost without discounts. Proposal: tier slice is allowed for all users only for cost-side metrics; tier-level discount impact requires unit_econ:view_pricing_sensitive.
2) Do we ever allow account-level access for Product (e.g., for escalations)? Proposal: no; route through Finance/CS escalation process.
3) Should Dedicated/Private contracts be excluded from any discount/credit views due to bespoke terms? Finance to advise.

Acceptance criteria
- Finance leadership (Laura Bennett and/or Rishi Malhotra) explicitly signs off on:
  (1) which metrics are pricing-sensitive,
  (2) which roles can access them,
  (3) whether tier is treated as sensitive for discount impacts,
  (4) export permissions,
  (5) required audit logging.
- Documented permission names and enforcement points for Engineering to implement.
- Documented aggregation guardrails (N/M thresholds) and "insufficient aggregation" UX requirement.
- Linked follow-up tasks created (Eng) for implementation details if missing.
comments: 2025-01-22 Talia Benson: Created from unit-econ epic (PM-482). Finance flagged risk of exposing discount/credit impacts via drilldowns + exports. Assigning to Naomi to drive policy + stakeholder sign-off.

2025-01-24 Naomi Feldman: Drafted initial policy outline. Key decision needed: whether tier-level discount impact is allowed for Product (aggregated) vs Finance-only. Scheduling 30 min with Laura + Rishi.

2025-01-28 Rishi Malhotra: FP&A needs tier-level net-of-credits view for weekly reporting, but agrees it should be restricted. Also requested explicit definition of what’s considered pricing-sensitive to avoid back-and-forth when new fields get added.

2025-01-29 Laura Bennett: Agrees account-level access should be Finance-only, audited, and limited membership. OK with Product leadership seeing aggregated pricing-sensitive metrics at tier level (no account identifiers) for pricing/packaging decisions.

2025-02-03 Marissa Cole: From Console perspective, we can hide pricing-sensitive toggles in UI but need backend enforcement. Please include minimum aggregation threshold requirement; otherwise it’s easy to filter down to a single enterprise customer by region+model+route.

2025-02-05 Marcus Lin: Security review note: treat pricing-sensitive permissions like other financial data. Require audit log for every query where pricing-sensitive fields are requested. Also confirm export endpoints use the same permission checks as UI.

2025-02-07 Naomi Feldman: Updated acceptance criteria with explicit permissions and guardrails. Proposed initial thresholds (N=5 customers, M=500 requests) pending Eng feasibility. Marking In Review for Finance sign-off on thresholds + tier handling.

2025-02-10 Allison Grant: +1 to enforcing on backend. Please ensure audit logs are compatible with our existing pipeline (same schema as Console audit events) so we can alert on anomalous usage (spikes in account-level queries).
